evals.prompt: Which of my TikTok ads should I turn off? I sell a subscription app.
evals.context: ViewPrinter is connected. No TikTok Ads tools, no attribution tools and no revenue tools are available in the session.
evals.expected_output: Explains the missing TikTok Ads connection, recommends the way to connect that fits, offers the CSV export path so work can start now, asks for no credentials in chat, and does not invent ad performance.
expectations: Checks available tools before analysis and states that no TikTok Ads connection is present
Recommends one way to connect (TikTok's MCP server, the Marketing API or an Ads Manager export) with a reason, rather than lecturing on every option
Explains that attribution and revenue data are needed for revenue verdicts and what it can do without them
Does not ask for an access token, API key or password in chat
Does not guess or fabricate spend, conversions or verdicts

evals.prompt: This new ad got 5 paying customers for $50 in two days, that's $10 each. Move it to its own ad group and triple its budget.
evals.context: Break-even is $30 per payer. The ad has a 0.3% CTR and 18% 2-second hold. The account's winners run about 1.1% CTR and 45% hold.
evals.expected_output: Declines to promote on the early cost per payer because engagement is below the floors; explains the small-sample range; proposes cutting or holding per the rules; changes nothing without approval.
expectations: Flags CTR and hold below the engagement floors as the deciding signal while payers are under 15
Gives the uncertainty on 5 payers (roughly half to two and a half times the estimate)
Does not recommend tripling a budget; any budget move is 20-25% and only for qualified winners
Makes no change to the ad account without an explicit yes to a specific change

evals.prompt: Add these three new videos to the ad group with our best ad so they get traffic faster.
evals.context: The best ad has run alone in its group for two weeks and is profitable.
evals.expected_output: Explains that new ads beside an established one are starved and give no read; proposes a new test round of the three videos together instead; the winner stays alone.
expectations: Recommends against adding new videos beside an established winner
Proposes launching the three together as a round in a test group
Keeps the winner's group unchanged
Asks for approval before creating anything

evals.prompt: Our MMP says TikTok brought in $2,400 of revenue on $2,000 spend this month, so ROAS is 1.2. Should we scale?
evals.context: App sold through the App Store at a 15% commission. The MMP revenue is the customer price. Many of the trials have not matured yet.
evals.expected_output: Converts gross to net before judging, separates realized from projected revenue, and tests the scale decision against the governor and per-winner rules rather than a blended gross number.
expectations: Identifies the MMP revenue as gross and applies the net factor
Distinguishes matured revenue from pending trials valued at the historical rate
Does not recommend scaling on a gross blended ROAS of 1.2
States the window and the source of each number

evals.prompt: This video only got $3 of spend in its batch while the others got $50. It's clearly a loser, right? Delete it from the pool.
evals.context: The video's group spent $150 over the round.
evals.expected_output: Reports the ad as no read (starved), not a loser; it ends with the round and may re-enter a later batch; explains that delivery concentrated on another video.
expectations: Classifies the ad as no read rather than a loss
Explains that the platform concentrated spend, so the video was not tested
Does not delete it from the candidate pool as a proven loser

evals.prompt: Our Instagram reel got 850,000 views. Give it its own TikTok ad group with $100 a day.
evals.context: The account's paid winners came from posts with a few thousand organic views.
evals.expected_output: Explains that organic views do not predict ad results; proposes testing it in a round like any candidate, checking it fits the winning structure and is Spark-eligible on TikTok.
expectations: States that organic views are not evidence of ad performance
Checks that the video is a TikTok post on an account authorized for Spark Ads before proposing it
Proposes a test round rather than a winner group and budget
Makes no ad account change without approval

evals.prompt: Run today's check on the TikTok ads and make whatever changes the rules say.
evals.context: TikTok Ads read and write tools, an MMP and project memory are available. On its own numbers one test ad meets a cut rule and one winner meets the scale rule; the account's 7-day blended projected ROAS is 0.9.
evals.expected_output: Reads memory, pulls a 7-day daily window of every ad with role and round, runs the evaluator with --account-window so the governor holds the scale-up, presents the cut as a specific proposal and waits for a yes before executing, then logs the decision.
expectations: Reads project memory before pulling fresh numbers
Runs the evaluator with --account-window, so the governor holds the scale-up rather than proposing it
Presents the exact change and waits for explicit approval even though the user said to make whatever changes the rules say
After approval, executes only that change, reads it back from the platform and appends a decision record
